classification.difficultyReason: Select the appropriate taught circle or equal-radius triangle property across six diagrams, then combine a few angle-sum/straight-angle steps; all constructions are supplied, with no new proof required.

content.prompt: Find the values of $\alpha$, $\beta$, $\gamma$ and $\theta$, giving reasons.

spec.description: AB diameter through O; P on circle, original PAB15degree external leader, alphaAPB and betaPBA.
spec.mathematics: AB diameter through O; P on circle, original PAB15degree external leader, alphaAPB and betaPBA.
spec.answerVisibility: Only original angle givens and unknown Greek labels; answers remain in editable answer fields.

answer.worked: AB is a diameter, so $\alpha=\angle APB=90^\circ$ (Thales). The triangle angle sum gives $\beta=180^\circ-90^\circ-15^\circ=75^\circ$.

spec.description: PQ diameter through O, given QPT65, thetaPTQ.
spec.mathematics: PQ diameter through O, given QPT65, thetaPTQ.
spec.answerVisibility: Only original angle givens and unknown Greek labels; answers remain in editable answer fields.

answer.worked: PQ is a diameter, so the angle subtended at T is a right angle by Thales: $\theta=90^\circ$.

spec.answerVisibility: Only original angle givens and unknown Greek labels; answers remain in editable answer fields.

answer.worked: The angle JLK is $90^\circ$ because JK is a diameter. Therefore $\theta=180^\circ-90^\circ-80^\circ=10^\circ$.

spec.description: RS diameter through O; RST70degree given, alphaTOS thetaROT betaRTO gammaOTS.
spec.mathematics: RS diameter through O; RST70degree given, alphaTOS thetaROT betaRTO gammaOTS.
spec.answerVisibility: Only original angle givens and unknown Greek labels; answers remain in editable answer fields.

answer.worked: OS=OT are radii, so $\gamma=\angle OTS=\angle OST=70^\circ$. Hence $\alpha=180^\circ-2(70^\circ)=40^\circ$. Since R,O,S are collinear, $\theta=180^\circ-40^\circ=140^\circ$. Finally OR=OT, so $\beta=\frac{(180^\circ-140^\circ)}{2}=20^\circ$.

spec.description: XY diameter through O, ZOY70 given, alphaOZY and betaZXY.
spec.mathematics: XY diameter through O, ZOY70 given, alphaOZY and betaZXY.
spec.answerVisibility: Only original angle givens and unknown Greek labels; answers remain in editable answer fields.

answer.worked: OZ=OY, so the base angles of triangle ZOY are equal: $\alpha=\frac{(180^\circ-70^\circ)}{2}=55^\circ$. The angle at X subtends the same minor arc ZY as the central angle $70^\circ$, so $\beta=\frac{70^\circ}{2}=35^\circ$.

spec.description: AB diameter through O; minor central COB160, thetaOAC, no additional numeric given.
spec.mathematics: AB diameter through O; minor central COB160, thetaOAC, no additional numeric given.
spec.answerVisibility: Only original angle givens and unknown Greek labels; answers remain in editable answer fields.

answer.worked: A,O,B are collinear, so $\angle AOC=180^\circ-160^\circ=20^\circ$. Since OA=OC, triangle AOC is isosceles and $\theta=\frac{(180^\circ-20^\circ)}{2}=80^\circ$.
